findings_addressed.oracle: Apply the generated patch back to the source via _call_apply_bps_patch and assert rebuilt == target (b'\x10\x11' * 1024). This independently recomputes the expected result using the BPS decoder as a second path, verifying the encoder produced a correct patch rather than just a correctly-magicked byte sequence.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py _build_bps_patch, change the SourceRead opcode encoding so it emits garbage data bytes instead of the correct source bytes — the round-trip assertion (rebuilt == target) will fail because the decoded target will contain wrong byte values.

notes: G0068 was a weak-existence check asserting only the BPS1 magic header. The hardened test now calls _call_apply_bps_patch with the generated patch and the original source, then asserts the result equals the expected target. Source=b'\x00\x01'*1024 and target=b'\x10\x11'*1024 are chosen so every byte differs, making it impossible for a broken encoder to accidentally produce a valid round-trip. The documented_mutation names a concrete change to _build_bps_patch that would make the rebuilt != target assertion fail.
